record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let M be a z-invariant subspace of L^2_a(D). Suppose N is another z-invariant subspace contained in M and maximal among proper invariant subspaces contained in M. Must N have codimension 1 inside M?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 17 Let M be an invariant subspace

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space, i.e., the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ for which $\|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\, dA(z) < \infty$, where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A closed subspace $M\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called $z$-invariant if $zf\in M$ for every $f\in M$.

Suppose $M\subseteq L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is a $z$-invariant subspace, and let $N\subsetneq M$ be a $z$-invariant subspace that is maximal among the proper $z$-invariant subspaces of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ contained in $M$ (that is, if $N'$ is a $z$-invariant subspace with $N\subseteq N'\subsetneq M$, then $N'=N$).

Must $N$ have codimension $1$ in $M$, i.e., must $\dim(M\ominus N)=1$?
artifact.status_search_result: Hedenmalm (1998) proved that every maximal proper invariant subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ itself has codimension 1, and subsequent work by Aleman–Richter and others established codimension-1 properties under various local conditions, with extensions to planar regions and abstract Fredholm-operator settings. However, no source directly confirming or refuting the relative version (with arbitrary ambient invariant subspace $M$) was located, so the status of this specific problem is unclear from the available search results.

status_evidence.title: Maximal invariant subspaces in the Bergman space (Hedenmalm)
status_evidence.snippet: Hedenmalm obtained that every maximal invariant subspace of the Bergman space is of codimension 1.
status_evidence.claim: The non-relative version (M = L^2_a) is solved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: The Codimension-1 Property in Bergman Spaces over Planar Regions
status_evidence.snippet: Aleman and Richter obtained local integrability conditions ensuring the codimension-1 property.
status_evidence.claim: Codimension-1 property has been studied locally and over planar regions, but the relative maximal version is not directly addressed.
